headline: Cloud growth outpaces costs, but restructuring dents profit
summary_short: Manhattan Associates grew Q2 FY2026 revenue 9.3% y/y to $297.8M on cloud-subscription demand (+26% y/y to $126.7M), but an $8.3M restructuring charge from a 6% headcount cut pulled operating margin down to 22.2% from 27.1% a year ago, and diluted EPS fell 8.6% y/y to $0.85.
summary_long: Revenue rose 9.3% y/y to $297.8M, led by cloud subscriptions revenue up 26% to $126.7M as customers keep migrating from on-premise to cloud; services revenue grew 3% while maintenance revenue (tied to legacy perpetual licenses) fell 13%. Cost of cloud/maintenance/services rose 11% on higher performance-based compensation, personnel costs, and infrastructure spend, and sales & marketing rose 54% on an expanded sales force. Operating margin fell to 22.2% from 27.1% on an $8.3M restructuring charge tied to a 6% headcount reduction plus the higher S&M spend. Net income fell 11.3% y/y to $50.4M ($0.85 diluted EPS, -8.6% y/y). Cash fell to $186.1M and equity fell to $157.5M after $275.0M of H1 buybacks; the board raised repurchase authority to $500M in March.

drivers.explanation: Strong cloud-subscription demand drove revenue growth, but an $8.3M restructuring charge (6% headcount cut) plus a bigger sales force pushed operating margin and EPS down y/y despite the higher revenue.
Cloud subscriptions revenue rose $26.3M in the quarter as customers keep migrating from on-premise to cloud-based offerings, with growth across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC segments.

The $13.0M quarterly increase reflects $4.7M higher performance-based compensation, $4.6M higher compensation/personnel costs, $2.6M higher computer infrastructure cost, and $1.1M higher travel costs.
Operating income and margin decreased primarily due to the restructuring expense as well as an increase in sales and marketing expenses.
Tracks the operating-income decline, partly offset by a $0.3M rise in other income from higher foreign-currency gains on intercompany balances.
Tracks the pretax-income decline; the effective tax rate also rose to 25.1% from 23.8%, which the filing attributes to a decrease in stock-based compensation tax benefits.
Tracks the net-income decline; diluted shares fell 3.4% y/y on continued buybacks, softening the per-share decline (-8.6%) relative to net income (-11.3%).
Tracks the net-income decline; basic shares fell on continued buybacks, softening the per-share decline (-8.5%) relative to net income (-11.3%).
Cash fell as $306.5M used for share repurchases and tax-withholding purchases in financing activities exceeded $174.7M of cash generated from operations.
Equity fell as $304.5M of H1 treasury-stock repurchases (per the equity statement) exceeded $99.6M of H1 net income.
Share count fell as the company repurchased approximately 1.9 million shares for $275.0M in H1 2026 under its buyback program.
